messages:
Iris: follow-up from today's all-hands runtime section: posting a short Q+A thread so we can track action items.

Diego: quick question	6 kernel autotune: how aggressive is the selector when profiles conflict (e.g., lower latency but slightly higher memory)?

Iris: selector uses weighted objectives: latency(0.6), memory(0.25), cost(0.15). if memory crosses a safety threshold (OOM risk), it will reject. we can tune weights per-customer later.

Sam: for the rollout controller, do we have a hard abort condition vs soft warning? want to know what triggers immediate rollback.

Iris: hard aborts: p99 > 2x baseline, token error-rate > 3x, OOM spikes. soft warnings: p95 > 1.25x, kv hit-rate drop > 15%. soft warnings surface in console and to oncall but don't auto-abort.

Nora: about batching: will we expose observed batch-size percentile metrics? SRE wants med/90/99.

Iris: yes	6 telemetry will include median/90/99 batch sizes, batching-wait-duration histograms, and per-route batching-config.

Diego: any note for customers about expected behavior change when adaptive-cache is enabled? I want a one-liner for release notes.

Iris: suggested line: "Adaptive prefix caching reduces repeated token costs and tail latency for many workloads; opt-out available via route settings." short + link to deep doc.

Sam: can we add a small canary YAML here so SRE can copy it?

Iris: paste below:

``` 
canary:
  phases:
    - pct: 1
      hold: 12h
    - pct: 10
      hold: 24h
signals:
  latency:
    p95_multiplier: 1.2
  errors:
    multiplier: 2.0
  mem:
    oom_rate_threshold: 0.01
```

Nora: great. I'll set up dashboards and the rollback playbook.

RollbackBot: rollout-controller: experiment/kernel-autotune-2026 created at 1800000450 :rocket:

Iris: thanks all	6 I'll collect these into the release thread + assign the doc owners for the deep dive.
